benefits.headline: A two-point credit if you have 2 to 11 points
benefits.body: Ohio Revised Code 4510.037 lets the registrar credit two points to a driver with at least two but fewer than twelve points who completes an approved remedial course. Once every three years, five times in a lifetime. The BMV's own words: completion "does not remove points from your record, but can act as a cushion against future convictions."

benefits.headline: One of the four reinstatement requirements after a 12-point suspension
benefits.body: Twelve or more points within two years is a six-month suspension. To reinstate, Ohio requires you to complete a remedial driving course, retake the complete driver license exam, file proof of financial responsibility (SR-22) for the period the BMV sets, and pay a reinstatement fee. We are the first of those four.

benefits.headline: A certificate that satisfies a court order
benefits.body: When a judge orders a remedial course, this course satisfies the order and you receive a certificate to file with the court. By statute a court-ordered completion earns no point credit.

faqs.q: Does the Ohio remedial course take points off my record?
faqs.a: No, and be wary of any course that says it does. The Ohio BMV states that completing the course "does not remove points from your record, but can act as a cushion against future convictions." The two-point credit raises the threshold at which a twelve-point suspension is triggered. Your convictions and their points stay on the record and remain visible to insurers.

faqs.q: Who qualifies for the two-point credit?
faqs.a: A driver with at least two but fewer than twelve points on their Ohio record, who has not used the credit in the past three years and has used it fewer than five times in their lifetime. A course taken under a judge's order earns no credit.

faqs.q: How often can I take it for the credit?
faqs.a: Once every three years, and five times in a lifetime. Ohio Revised Code 4510.037 sets both limits.

faqs.q: I got a 12-point suspension. Is this the course I need?
faqs.a: Yes. After a twelve-point suspension Ohio requires an approved remedial driving course, a retake of the complete driver license exam, proof of financial responsibility on file with the BMV, and a reinstatement fee. This course satisfies the first requirement. The other three happen at the BMV.

faqs.q: How long does the course take?
faqs.a: Eight hours of measured instruction. Ohio credits only real time on the content, so the timer is on screen the whole way and break time is not counted. Most people finish across three or four sittings.

faqs.q: How long do I have to finish?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the date and time you first open the course content, set by Ohio Administrative Code 4501-21-14. After thirty days Ohio requires the course to start again. The clock starts when you open Module 1, not when you pay.

faqs.q: What is the final exam like?
faqs.a: Forty questions drawn from a state-required bank of at least 120, graded when you finish, 75% to pass. Course content is locked while the exam is open. If you miss it, you get one retake no sooner than 24 hours later, and we email you the moment it unlocks.

faqs.q: What if I fail the exam twice?
faqs.a: Ohio's rule is that a second failure means retaking the course. We tell you that here rather than at the end. The unit knowledge checks are built to make sure you are ready before you ever see the final.

Ohio requires an identity check after every two hours of instruction and before the final exam. You answer a question only you would know. A wrong answer gives you one more try; a second wrong answer locks the course for 24 hours, by state rule. Answer honestly and it takes ten seconds.

faqs.q: When do I get my certificate?
faqs.a: After you pass, we enter your completion in Ohio's DETS system, which is linked to the BMV, and email you the signed certificate PDF. Certificates are issued by our staff during support hours, usually the same business day. Keep your copy: local courts cannot see the state record.
Yes. The certificate, the DETS entry, one exam retake, audio narration and support are all inside that number. There is no processing fee and no upgraded version of the course.
Yes, in full, at any time before you complete the course. Once you have passed the exam and the certificate is issued there is no refund, because it has already been earned and reported.

We do not promise that. Ohio's statutory premium reduction for mature drivers applies only to courses with classroom instruction, which this is not. Some insurers run their own programs; ask yours before you enroll if that is your reason.

faqs.q: Can I do this on my phone?
faqs.a: Yes. The course, the timer and the exam all work on a phone. Your progress saves the moment you leave, so ten minutes on a break counts toward your eight hours.

faqs.q: Is the course live or on a schedule?
faqs.a: No. It is entirely self-paced and asynchronous. There are no sessions to attend and no one to wait for. That is how Ohio defines an online course.
